chunks: Yūnus, from Abān ibn Taghlib, from one who narrated it, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“When a slave kills a free man, he is handed over to the heirs of the slain person. If they wish, they may kill him; if they wish, they may detain him so that he becomes a slave belonging to them; and if they wish, they may enslave him.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ: the heirs or legal guardians of the slain person who hold the right of response
key_terms.اسْتَرَقُّوهُ: they may enslave him; take him into slavery
key_terms.الْحُرَّ: the free person; the victim whose legal status affects the ruling
key_terms.الْعَبْدُ: the slave; the offender in this legal case
key_terms.حَبَسُوهُ: they may detain him and hold him under their possession
key_terms.عَبْدًا لَهُمْ: a slave belonging to them; under their ownership
key_terms.قَتَلُوهُ: they may kill him; exercise retaliation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave kills a free man in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning retaliation and the options available to the heirs of a free person killed by a slave. It outlines their authority over the offender, including execution, detention as their slave, or enslavement, within the framework of judicial rulings in cases of homicide.
